name: Hori
title: Horite patriarch and descendant of Simeon
summary: Hori is a name that appears twice in the Bible. One is a Horite patriarch, son of Lotan and a descendant of Seir in the land of Edom. The other is the father of Shaphat, one of the spies from the tribe of Simeon sent into Canaan. Both are mentioned in genealogies and lists without further narrative detail.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Seir's Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Hori is mentioned as the son of Lotan, grandson of Seir the Horite, among the original inhabitants of the land of Edom.

keyEvents.title: Horite Chiefs in the Land of Seir
keyEvents.description: Hori is listed among the descendants of the Horites who lived in the land of Seir before Esau's descendants took over the area.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: The genealogy of Seir with Hori as the son of Lotan is repeated in 1 Chronicles as part of Edom's genealogy.

keyEvents.title: Hori as the father of the spy Shaphat
keyEvents.description: Another Hori is mentioned as the father of Shaphat from the tribe of Simeon, one of the twelve spies Moses sent to explore the land of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: The sons of Seir and Edom's prehistory
keyEvents.description: The Horites, including Hori, represent the original inhabitants of the mountains of Seir before Esau's descendants drove them out and settled there.
